text:
ana: ran the tracebench for the new batch formation heuristic (qpolicy-v3) on the 03/10 traces. posting the condensed findings.
tracebot: automated-run: tracebench://runs/1896001111 completed (duration 27m). configs: qpolicy-v3, token_budget_target=384, kv_prefetch=0.6, kernel_hints=auto. artifacts -> s3://redwood-tracebench/1896001111/
ana: TL;DR: p50 latency -5.8%, p95 -12.3% vs baseline (qpolicy-v2). throughput (tokens/s) -7.1% under peak due to slightly longer batching build times. KV warmup hit rate +18% for long-lived sessions.
sam: curious — why did throughput drop? was kernel selection different?
ana: two things: v3 increases wait window for short requests to form denser batches (helps latency variance) which raises queuing during spikes. second, kernel_hints=auto flipped to aten-fused for some transformer blocks; those kernels have higher per-batch startup cost on the 80-token median traces.
liam: can you paste the exact command you ran and the key metrics?
ana: sure:
```
./tools/tracebench run --policy qpolicy-v3 --trace traces/2026-03-10.json \
  --sim-params "token_budget=384,kv_prefetch=0.6,kernel_hints=auto" \
  --ab-group A --ab-group B:baseline
```
Metrics (aggregated): p50: 28ms -> 26.4ms, p95: 120ms -> 105.4ms, tokens/s peak: 540k -> 502k. kv hit rate: 62% -> 73%.
rachel: A/B harness (offline eval over 50k sessions) shows user-visible regressions ~0.6% in completion time tail for chat workloads that have many short messages. but reranking workloads improved 1.9% overall.
sam: ok, so tradeoff is tail latency for short-message-heavy apps. Any easy knobs to recover throughput without losing latency gains?
ana: a few experiments looked promising: 1) dynamic token_budget per-model: decrease to 256 for small chat models to reduce queue hold time; 2) hybrid kernel policy: force low-latency kernels when batch size < X; 3) adaptive prefetch ramp (start kv_prefetch at 0.3 then ramp to 0.7 after warmup).
liam: did tracebench simulate KV cold starts? how sensitive is the perf to cold-key miss rates?
ana: yes, we replayed traces with synthetic cold-start injection (10% sessions artificially reset). With cold starts, p95 regressions were bigger on v3 (~+18ms) but hybrid kernel + kv ramp reduced that to +4ms.
tracebot: artifact links: s3://redwood-tracebench/1896001111/logs.tar.gz, s3://redwood-tracebench/1896001111/ab_results.csv
sam: actionable plan: roll v3 to canary with token_budget override -> 256 for chat models; enable hybrid kernel short-batch fallback; monitor p95 and tokens/s for 24h. agree? :thumbsup:
rachel: +1. I'll add the A/B gating thresholds to the dashboard (p95 delta threshold 5% for automatic rollback).
liam: I'll add a microbenchmark for kernel startup cost across seq len distribution. want the numbers before canary.
ana: thanks team. I'll open a PR with the config toggles and a short runbook for canary. filing follow-ups in the perf epic.
